profile.summary: Genomics-FM is a DNA foundation model meant to cut the amount of labelled data that genomic prediction tasks need. It is a BERT-style encoder pretrained on large amounts of unlabelled DNA with an ensemble of tokenisation vocabularies (BPE and 6-mer), then fine-tuned with one task-specific vocabulary on a small labelled set. The authors apply it to genome annotation, epigenomic and expression profile prediction, and variant effect assessment.

summary_quotes.text: the development of AI models needs substantial labeled data, and these models are typically task-specific with limited generalizability to various applications

Genomics-FM is first pretrained with ensemble genomic vocabulary on vast unlabelled data to learn comprehensive and generalizable representations and then finetuned with specific genomic vocabulary on limited labeled data
including genome annotation, epigenomic and expression profile prediction, and variant effect assessment

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The model is a BERT masked language model built on the MosaicML BERT code, which uses ALiBi position biases and FlashAttention. During pretraining each sequence is tokenised either with a BPE vocabulary or as 6-mers, and a prompt token marking the vocabulary ([BPE] or [KMER]) and the position scheme ([ALIBI] or [APE]) is put in front of it. Sequences are randomly replaced by their reverse complement half the time. Training masks tokens with a probability of 0.15 for BPE input and 0.15 divided by 6 for 6-mer input, over blocks of 512 tokens, for up to 1,000,000 steps in fp16. For a downstream task the model is fine-tuned with one chosen vocabulary.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The README offers one checkpoint folder on Google Drive, with no version label or checksum. The model configuration file the pretraining script expects (config/config_prompt.json) is not in the repository, so the exact architecture size cannot be read from the code. The README recommends PyTorch 1.7.1 with CUDA 11.0, verified on a 3090 GPU cluster. A result should record the Drive file used and the repository commit; this page read commit edc9f16b.

quotes.text: Personally, I recommend fresh students use some stable version of Pytorch to match 3090 GPU cluster such as 1.7.1, which has been verified.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: BERT-style genomic foundation model trained by masked language modelling with multiple tokenisation vocabularies.

quotes.text: a genomic vocabulary driven foundation model

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Transformer encoder from the MosaicML BERT code, with ALiBi and FlashAttention support. Layer count and width are not given in the repository (the config file is missing).

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: DNA sequence, tokenised either by BPE or as 6-mers, with a prompt token naming the vocabulary and position scheme in front.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Masked-token predictions in pretraining; task predictions after fine-tuning (genome annotation, epigenomic and expression profiles, variant effects). No inference code is published.

quotes.text: genome annotation, epigenomic and expression profile prediction, and variant effect assessment

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: Not stated by the developers in the sources read. GENEB, a third-party benchmark, lists 120M.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: Not extracted. The abstract says vast unlabelled data; the launch script leaves the training file paths blank and records 298,018,034 training samples. GENEB describes the data as multi-species.

facts.value: Not stated. The repository has no licence file; individual files carry Apache-2.0 headers from the code they were adapted from (MosaicML, Hugging Face).

strengths.text: Designed for tasks with little labelled data: the authors report it reduces dependence on labels and shows some zero-shot prediction across species and tissues. These are the developers' claims.

quotes.text: We show that Genomics-FM significantly reduces the dependence on labeled data
Genomics-FM even shows impressive zero-shot predictive capabilities across diverse species and tissues

strengths.text: One pretrained model serves more than one tokenisation (BPE and 6-mer), so the vocabulary can be chosen per task at fine-tuning.

limitations.text: No inference or fine-tuning instructions are published: the README covers installation and a checkpoint link only.
Weights are only on Google Drive, with no version, checksum or licence, and the model configuration file is not in the repository.
The software stack is old and GPU-oriented: PyTorch 1.7.1 with CUDA 11.0, optional NVIDIA apex for fp16, and pretraining launched with srun on a cluster.

quotes.text: Install the apex requirements (Optional, install apex for fp16 training)

no_run_guide_reason: The README covers environment setup and a Google Drive checkpoint link only. The repository has no inference or fine-tuning script, and the configuration file the code expects is missing, so a run guide would have to invent commands.
notes: The README title is spelled 'Geomics-FM'. GENEB vendors a copy of this code (embedding_pipeline/utility_modules/genomicsfm_project) and lists Genomics-FM as 120M, multi-species; its extractor was not treated as developer instructions. Coverage is limited because there is no model card and only the abstract of the paper was read.
